_feeds_comment: BROAD NEWS, NOT JUST YOUR TICKERS. A per-symbol feed can only ever mention a company already on your list, so it cannot warn you about a Fed decision, a Hormuz closure or an election result — the things that move holdings without naming them. Official sources are listed first on purpose: a central bank's own statement is the thing itself, where a news story about it is a report of it. Delete any that get noisy. Every fetch reports its own failure, so a dead feed is named in the letter.
_feed_limit: headlines taken per feed. Higher costs a little more to summarise.
_positions_name_comment: `name` is what a NEWS SEARCH is given, not a label. A bare ticker is a low-precision query dressed as a targeted one — searching 'VOO' or 'ALL' returns English rather than news — so a symbol with no name here skips the Google News rung and reports `no_name` instead of serving noise as coverage.
_feeds_dead_comment: US Treasury (home.treasury.gov/rss/press.xml) and White House (whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/feed/) were REMOVED on 2026-09-22: both 404 from a hosted runner, and so did the obvious alternative path for each. A 404 is a path that does not exist, which makes it ours; but a replacement nobody has seen answer is a guess, and a feed that fails every run is noise in the letter's data notes. Put either back the moment a URL is seen returning items. Yahoo S&P 500 went the same way on the same day, for the OTHER reason: http_429 on every run, because Yahoo fences datacentres as a block. It works from a laptop and never from the runner this lives on, and MarketWatch and CNBC already carry the index's news. Eleven feeds left.
_new_thresholds_comment: BOT 8% and OUST 10% are STARTING GUESSES, not measurements. CELH's 8% was set the same way and the reasoning is in triggers.movers: a threshold too low sends a small cap's ordinary Tuesday every week, and the response to that is muting the channel the dip alerts share. Both should be re-set from their own realised daily ranges once there are a few weeks of collected prices to measure. HOOD 10% AND AMZN'S ABSENCE ARE MEASURED, NOT GUESSED (2026-10-02, from 1,293 and 2,530 daily closes in stocks_model): HOOD's median absolute daily move is 2.50% and its p95 is 8.79%, so the 5% default would fire on 18.5% of days — 47 times a year, which is exactly the ordinary-Tuesday flood that gets a channel muted; 10% fires on 3.6% of days, about nine times a year. AMZN's median is 1.08% and p95 4.15%, so the 5% default already fires only 3.0% of days and an override would be noise about noise. BE 8% and NAUT 12% ARE STILL GUESSES — neither has a single close in the store, because neither is in the S&P 500 and that is the only universe collected. NAUT trades near $2, where a ten-cent wobble is 5%. Re-set both from their own realised ranges once prices exist.
_bot_nav_comment: BOT IS A CLOSED-END FUND, NOT AN ETF — confirmed on the runner 2026-09-22 (TradingView type 'fund', typespecs ['closedend']; Nasdaq answers 'Symbol not exists' for assetclass=etf). No creation/redemption at NAV, so nothing pulls the price back to the assets and the premium is structural. THE NAV COMES FROM CEF CONNECT, whose own figures read: 2026-06-30 NAV 10.51 against a price of 39.75, a premium of +278%; 2026-07-31 NAV 11.32 against 25.98, +130%. It is a QUARTERLY APPRAISAL of private holdings, so between marks the premium moves because the PRICE moved, not because anything was re-valued — nav_cadence says so and the letter repeats it every time. premium_rungs_pct: +100 WARNS and is not a buy; 50, 25 and 0 are the levels. They are spaced by the loss taken if the premium converges — p/(1+p) — so +50 means a 33% fall to reach NAV. None of the positive rungs is an endorsement; the closed-end base rate says the defensible entry is at or below NAV. Change them here, not in code.
_shares_comment: SHARES ARE WHAT TURNS A PRICE LIST INTO A BOOK. With them the letter can say what a position is WORTH and what WEIGHT it carries, which is the number that argues against buying more — a green ticker never does. Transcribed from the brokerage screenshot of 2026-10-02; this file is the only record, so edit it after a trade or the weights go stale silently. A position with no `shares` key is still priced and still alerted, and is reported as UNSIZED rather than counted as zero: BTC-USD has no figure here because the screenshot was the Stocks & ETFs tab only, and treating that as zero would understate the book and overstate every weight in it.
